description.narrative: In all affected governates across the whole of Syria, specially in the Northeast

SARC supported by the IFRC, is implementing a comprehensive response focused on the following actions: Emergency Medical Services: SARC volunteers are actively transporting the injured to national hospitals and providing trauma care. Assistance to People on the Move: Teams are stationed at transit points to provide humanitarian assistance and protection to those fleeing the hostilities. Relief Distribution: Several trucks carrying essential relief items have been dispatched to the affected governorates to address immediate survival needs. Preparedness and Mitigation: The plan includes scaling up preparedness actions to manage further mass displacements and mitigating the impacts of extreme weather through site improvements and essential supply replenishment.

Syria is experiencing a disruption and an escalation in humanitarian needs following a major shift in hostilities in the North and Northeast. Please find attached the Since early January 2026, shifting territorial control and intensified conflict have led to mass displacement across the Aleppo, Ar-Raqqa, Deir Ez-Zor, and Al-Hasakeh governorates. This surge in violence has fundamentally altered the scope and scale of the existing emergency. Please find attached the extended flash update, which serves as an update of the also attached EA for Syria Complex Emergency, expanding its scope and reach.

The protracted crisis in Syria over the past 13 years and the fragile humanitarian situation have now deepened significantly following intensified hostilities and rapid developments since 28 November 2024. The escalation resulted in mass displacement, destruction of critical infrastructure, and significant humanitarian needs. Over 1.1 million people have been displaced, with the potential for up to 1.5 million more if the violence continues. Many families are seeking shelter in overcrowded and underserved areas, and reports indicate significant civilian casualties, injuries, and shortages of food. Access to healthcare, protection, livelihoods, and basic services has been severely restricted due to ongoing hostilities and insecurity.
